text:
sylvie: Heads up — eu-south1 control-plane rollout (config v4.2.1) appears stuck. Seeing a bunch of auth failures and console 502s since ~09:02 UTC. Anyone else?
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-20260318-0452 · Severity: P2 · assigned to oncall (raj) :rotating_light:
raj: I'm on it. Pulling control-plane logs and etcd metrics now. First guess: config change that touched auth-proxy routing table.
maria: Confirming 502s from the console in eu-south1, and a spike in 401s from downstream services. Token validation errors: "jwt: signature invalid" in gateway logs.
kevin: deploy-bot shows partial rollout — 4/12 control-plane nodes upgraded, several now in CrashLoopBackOff. deploy-bot: "rollout failed on nodes: cp-03, cp-07, cp-09"
dana: Can you paste the failing pod logs?
raj: Pasted snippets — short tail:```
2026-03-18T09:02:13Z gateway auth-proxy error: unable to fetch signing keys: timeout contacting kms-service
2026-03-18T09:02:18Z auth-service warn: token validation failed: kid not found in jwks
2026-03-18T09:02:21Z controlplane cfg-sync error: apply config v4.2.1: failed to update route table: conflict: checksum mismatch
```
sylvie: @maria did we change jwks rotation or endpoint config in 4.2.1?
maria: Yes — the rollout switched auth-proxy to use the jwks endpoint behind the new control-plane cert (rotation). We tested in staging but not with fleet peer cert caching toggles.
kevin: Looks like nodes that rolled already are attempting to reach the new jwks endpoint but the load-balancer is routing them to old control-plane instances that don't have the new cert — TLS handshake fails and then token keys are unavailable.
dana: If true we should pause rollouts and shift traffic away from eu-south1 to avoid customer impact. Cost note: shifting heavy inference traffic to NA/west will spin up extra capacity; expected burst cost ~+$6k/day if we hold for 24h.
raj: Agreed — pausing rollout now. Command:```
deployctl rollout pause --cluster eu-south1 --config v4.2.1
Result: rollout paused. 5 nodes still pending.
```
maria: I'll trigger a manual rollback of the cert toggle in the config and re-run jwks service to serve both certs while we reconcile LB routing.
kevin: Prep for traffic shift — want to do gradual shift for customer segments 0-75% to west1. Using router policy update:```
redwood-router update --region eu-south1 --fallback-region na-west1 --weight 30
redwood-router update --region eu-south1 --fallback-region na-west1 --weight 60
redwood-router update --region eu-south1 --fallback-region na-west1 --weight 100
```
ops-bot: oncall (raj) marked incident as "mitigating" · started at 09:14 UTC
raj: Executing first step now — shifting 30% to na-west1. Monitoring auth errors and token error rate.
kevin: After shift -> token error rate dropped ~78% and console 502s reduced. Still seeing 401s for a small subset pinned sessions.
dana: I'll open a capacity request to infra for temporary +4 GPU nodes in na-west1 to keep latency acceptable for shifted traffic. Infra cost owner FYI: billing spike expected.
maria: Rolling back cert toggle to v4.2.0 in eu-south1 and restarting jwks-service:```
redwoodctl config apply --cluster eu-south1 --file jwks-backcompat.yaml --dry-run=false
systemctl restart jwks-service
```
sylvie: Good. Once jwks-service is back serving old and new keys, we can resume and finish a controlled rollout with LB fix. Who will own the LB mapping change?
kevin: I'll coordinate with netops. Plan: ensure LB has correct SNI mapping and sticky routing to nodes that have the updated cert, then resume gradual rollout. ETA for LB fix ~45m.
oncall-bot: Reminder — please update the incident doc with timeline + customer impact (customers: enterprise accounts in eu-south1 may see increased latency).
raj: I'll update the incident doc and keep watch. Current status: traffic partially shifted (30%), rollout paused, jwks rolled back, LB fix in progress. Next update in 20m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
